svg.title: What the Soil Decides: Septic Cost Funnel
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-septic-cost-funnel; chapter number: 6; chart type: funnel; title: What the Soil Decides: Septic Cost Funnel; subtitle: Upper-bound cost of each system tier down to the perc test that sorts them; caption: A perc test costing at most $1,500 is the gate that decides whether a parcel needs a conventional system or an alternative system that can run to $60,000, which is why practitioners test first and buy second.; assumptions note: Each stage value is the upper end of the cost range reported by the cited practitioners; the display field shows the full reported range. Stages narrow by reported cost, not by parcel counts.; note: Attributed to Jack Bosch (nVJMPjUWdZw), Florida Land Facts (zWTn3NY8wqc), Seth Williams of REtipster (yp6qPMTkjgE), the Apke Brothers (j3-xqUjgb7k), and Groundwork (dSAQlt9llvM).; stages: label: Alternative Systems (Mound, ATU, Drip); value: 60000; display: $15,000-$60,000; conversion: Triggered when soil fails a conventional design; detail: Mounds, treatment units, and drip systems run roughly $15,000 to $60,000 per land and septic practitioners.; label: Bosch Deal-Killer Tier; value: 50000; display: $30,000-$50,000; conversion: Kills a $5,000 lot meant for a $30,000 mobile home; detail: Jack Bosch prices the system the soil demands against the end buyer's build budget before committing.; label: Conventional System; value: 20000; display: $5,000-$20,000; conversion: Default path when the perc passes; detail: Conventional systems run roughly $5,000 to $20,000.; label: Florida Conventional Install; value: 15000; display: $10,000-$15,000; conversion: Often more than an $8,000 lot; detail: Florida Land Facts cites $3,600 to $12,500 nationally, with Florida installs usually landing at $10,000 to $15,000.; label: County Perc Test; value: 1500; display: $150-$1,500; conversion: Run inside due diligence, never after closing; detail: Seth Williams reports county health departments typically charge $150 to $1,500; the Apke Brothers cap standard diligence at 48 hours.

text.title: What the Soil Decides: Septic Cost Funnel
text.tspan: What the Soil Decides: Septic Cost Funnel

circle.title: label: Alternative Systems (Mound, ATU, Drip); value: 60000; display: $15,000-$60,000; conversion: Triggered when soil fails a conventional design; detail: Mounds, treatment units, and drip systems run roughly $15,000 to $60,000 per land and septic practitioners.

label: Bosch Deal-Killer Tier; value: 50000; display: $30,000-$50,000; conversion: Kills a $5,000 lot meant for a $30,000 mobile home; detail: Jack Bosch prices the system the soil demands against the end buyer's build budget before committing.
label: Conventional System; value: 20000; display: $5,000-$20,000; conversion: Default path when the perc passes; detail: Conventional systems run roughly $5,000 to $20,000.

label: Florida Conventional Install; value: 15000; display: $10,000-$15,000; conversion: Often more than an $8,000 lot; detail: Florida Land Facts cites $3,600 to $12,500 nationally, with Florida installs usually landing at $10,000 to $15,000.

label: County Perc Test; value: 1500; display: $150-$1,500; conversion: Run inside due diligence, never after closing; detail: Seth Williams reports county health departments typically charge $150 to $1,500; the Apke Brothers cap standard diligence at 48 hours.

text.title: Assumptions: Each stage value is the upper end of the cost range reported by the cited practitioners; the display field shows the full reported range. Stages narrow by reported cost, not by parcel counts.
